passages.excerpt_preview: It describes Bose’s early twentieth-century studies of electrical response and transmission in plants, including Mimosa and Desmodium, and his use of instruments to record changes too small to observe directly.
The authors call the work pioneering and connect it to later interest in plant electrophysiology.
he review notes that John Burdon-Sanderson had demonstrated action potentials in Venus flytrap before Bose’s program.
Their claim that later work confirmed most of Bose’s observations is a modern review interpretation, not a substitute for re-evaluating each historical experiment.
